ddl:
CREATE TABLE if not exists Region (
  postal_code varchar(10) PRIMARY KEY, 
  state varchar(50) not null, 
  country varchar(50) not null
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists Address (
  address_id bigint PRIMARY KEY, 
  building_num int, 
  street varchar(50), 
  city varchar(50), 
  postal_code varchar(10) not null,
  FOREIGN KEY (postal_code) REFERENCES Region(postal_code) on delete cascade
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists Publisher (
  publisher_id int PRIMARY KEY, 
  name varchar(50) not null, 
  email varchar(50), 
  phone_number bigint not null, 
  address_id bigint,
  FOREIGN KEY (address_id) REFERENCES Address(address_id) on delete set null
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists Book (
  ISBN varchar(30) PRIMARY KEY, 
  title varchar(50) not null, 
  author_name varchar(50) not null, 
  genre varchar(30) not null, 
  publisher_id int not null, 
  number_of_pages int not null, 
  cost numeric(4, 2) not null, 
  price numeric(4, 2) not null, 
  publisher_percent numeric(4, 2) not null, 
  stock int not null, 
  threshold int not null, 
  FOREIGN KEY (publisher_id) REFERENCES Publisher(publisher_id) on delete cascade
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists Staff (
  staff_id int PRIMARY KEY, 
  email varchar(50) not null
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists Warehouse (
  warehouse_id int PRIMARY KEY, 
  address_id bigint, 
  FOREIGN KEY (address_id) REFERENCES Address(address_id) on delete set null
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists Client (
  client_id int PRIMARY KEY auto_increment, 
  name varchar(50) not null, 
  email varchar(50) not null, 
  phone_number bigint, 
  address_id bigint, 
  FOREIGN KEY (address_id) REFERENCES Address(address_id) on delete set null
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists BankAccount (
  account_number int PRIMARY KEY, 
  amount numeric(12, 2) not null
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists Sales (
  ISBN varchar(30), 
  month varchar(20) check ( month in ('January', 'February', 'March', 'April', 'May', 'June', 'July', 'August', 'September', 'October', 'November', 'December')), 
  year int check (year > 1900 and year < 2022), 
  quantity int not null, 
  PRIMARY KEY (ISBN, month, year), 
  FOREIGN KEY (ISBN) REFERENCES Book(ISBN) on delete cascade
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists Orders (
  order_number int PRIMARY KEY auto_increment, 
  order_placement_date timestamp not null, 
  status varchar(15) check ( status in ('PENDING', 'SHIPPED', 'ARRIVED')), 
  final_total Numeric(12, 2) not null, 
  address_id bigint not null, 
  warehouse_id int not null,
  FOREIGN KEY (address_id) REFERENCES Address(address_id) on delete cascade, 
  FOREIGN KEY (warehouse_id) REFERENCES Warehouse(warehouse_id) on delete cascade
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists manage (
  ISBN varchar(30), 
  staff_id int, 
  PRIMARY KEY (ISBN, staff_id), 
  FOREIGN KEY (ISBN) REFERENCES Book(ISBN) on delete cascade, 
  FOREIGN KEY (staff_id) REFERENCES Staff(staff_id) on delete cascade
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists update_sales (
  order_number int, 
  ISBN varchar(30), 
  month varchar(20) check ( month in ('January', 'February', 'March', 'April', 'May', 'June', 'July', 'August', 'September', 'October', 'November', 'December')), 
  year int check (year > 1900 and year < 2022), 
  PRIMARY KEY (order_number, ISBN, month, year), 
  FOREIGN KEY (order_number) REFERENCES Orders(order_number) on delete cascade, 
  FOREIGN KEY (ISBN, month, year) REFERENCES Sales(ISBN, month, year) on delete cascade
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists handle_account (
  order_number int, 
  account_number int, 
  PRIMARY KEY (order_number, account_number), 
  FOREIGN KEY (order_number) REFERENCES Orders(order_number) on delete cascade, 
  FOREIGN KEY (account_number) REFERENCES BankAccount(account_number) on delete cascade
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists client_account (
  client_id int, 
  account_number int, 
  PRIMARY KEY (client_id, account_number), 
  FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES Client(client_id) on delete cascade, 
  FOREIGN KEY (account_number) REFERENCES BankAccount(account_number) on delete cascade
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists publisher_account (
  publisher_id int PRIMARY KEY, 
  account_number int,
  FOREIGN KEY (publisher_id) REFERENCES Publisher(publisher_id) on delete cascade, 
  FOREIGN KEY (account_number) REFERENCES BankAccount(account_number) on delete cascade
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists tracks (
  order_number int PRIMARY KEY auto_increment, 
  client_id int,
  FOREIGN KEY (order_number) REFERENCES Orders(order_number) on delete cascade, 
  FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES Client(client_id) on delete cascade
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists emails (
  staff_id int, 
  publisher_id int, 
  PRIMARY KEY (staff_id, publisher_id), 
  FOREIGN KEY (staff_id) REFERENCES Staff(staff_id) on delete cascade, 
  FOREIGN KEY (publisher_id) REFERENCES Publisher(publisher_id) on delete cascade
);
CREATE TABLE if not exists checkout (
  ISBN varchar(30), 
  order_number int, 
  quantity int, 
  PRIMARY KEY (ISBN, order_number), 
  FOREIGN KEY (ISBN) REFERENCES Book(ISBN) on delete cascade, 
  FOREIGN KEY (order_number) REFERENCES Orders(order_number) on delete cascade
);

Background / Context

Liber is an online bookstore platform developed using PHP, designed to allow users to browse, search, and order books online. The system integrates various functionalities for both customers and bookstore staff to enhance the browsing, purchasing, and management of books.

 Objectives

The primary goal of the Liber system is to provide a user-friendly online environment for book enthusiasts to discover and purchase books while offering management capabilities for bookstore staff. The platform aims to improve accessibility to books and streamline the sales and inventory processes.

 Stakeholders & Users

- Customers: Individuals who will browse the bookstore, search for books, and place orders.
- Bookstore Staff: Employees responsible for managing book inventories and generating sales reports.
- Publishers: Entities collaborating with the bookstore for publication and distribution agreements.

 Functional Descriptions

1. Browsing & Searching:  
   - Customers can browse available books.
   - Users can search books by title, ISBN, author name, and genre.

2. Ordering:
   - Customers can add books to a cart and place orders for home delivery.
   - Orders include tracking features with statuses like 'PENDING', 'SHIPPED', and 'ARRIVED'.

3. Inventory Management:  
   - Staff can modify book details including stock updates.
   - System allows management of inventory levels and alerts at thresholds.

4. Sales Reporting:
   - Generate sales reports based on monthly and yearly data.

5. Payment Processing:
   - Supports transactions through client bank accounts securely.

6. Publisher Management:
   - Handle publisher relationships and account information.

 Non-Functional Descriptions

- Scalability: Support a growing inventory of books and user base efficiently.
- Security: Ensure secure handling of customer data and payment processing.
- Usability: Provide an intuitive user interface for easy navigation and operation by both customers and staff.
- Data Integrity: Maintain consistent and accurate data across all tables and operations, ensuring robust relational integrity.

The schemabench_0169 database is a comprehensive schema for a bookstore management system. It consists of 18 tables, each representing a different entity or relationship in the system.
The Region table contains postal codes and their corresponding states and countries, which are used to identify the location of a particular address.
The Address table contains information about the physical address of a publisher, warehouse, or client. It includes the address ID, building number, street, city, postal code, and foreign key references to the Region table.
The Publisher table contains information about the publishers of books in the system. It includes the publisher ID, name, email, phone number, and address ID, as well as foreign key references to the Address table.
The Book table contains information about the books in the system. It includes the ISBN, title, author name, genre, publisher ID, number of pages, cost, price, publisher percentage, stock, and threshold. It also includes foreign key references to the Publisher table.
The Staff table contains information about the staff members in the system. It includes the staff ID and email.
The Warehouse table contains information about the warehouses in the system. It includes the warehouse ID and address ID, as well as foreign key references to the Address table.
The Client table contains information about the clients in the system. It includes the client ID, name, email, phone number, and address ID, as well as foreign key references to the Address table.
The BankAccount table contains information about the bank accounts in the system. It includes the account number and amount.
The Sales table contains information about the sales of books in the system. It includes the ISBN, month, year, quantity, and foreign key references to the Book table.
The Orders table contains information about the orders placed by clients in the system. It includes the order number, order placement date, status, final total, address ID, and warehouse ID, as well as foreign key references to the Address and Warehouse tables.
The manage table contains information about the books managed by staff members in the system. It includes the ISBN, staff ID, and foreign key references to the Book and Staff tables.
The update_sales table contains information about the sales of books in the system, including the order number, ISBN, month, year, and quantity, as well as foreign key references to the Orders and Sales tables.
The handle_account table contains information about the bank accounts associated with orders in the system. It includes the order number and account number, as well as foreign key references to the Orders and BankAccount tables.
The client_account table contains information about the bank accounts associated with clients in the system. It includes the client ID and account number, as well as foreign key references to the Client and BankAccount tables.
The publisher_account table contains information about the bank accounts associated with publishers in the system. It includes the publisher ID and account number, as well as foreign key references to the Publisher and BankAccount tables.
The tracks table contains information about the tracking of orders in the system. It includes the order number and client ID, as well as foreign key references to the Orders and Client tables.
The emails table contains information about the emails sent to staff members and publishers in the system. It includes the staff ID and publisher ID, as well as foreign key references to the Staff and Publisher tables.
The checkout table contains information about the books checked out by clients in the system. It includes the ISBN, order number, and quantity, as well as foreign key references to the Book and Orders tables.
Overall, the schemabench_0169 database schema provides a comprehensive framework for managing a bookstore management system, including information about publishers, books, clients, orders, and sales. It also includes information about the physical locations of publishers, warehouses, and clients, as well as the bank accounts associated with these entities.
